title: ADA/ABA Accessibility Guidelines — US federal (machine-extracted)
basis: Machine-extracted from the eCFR versioner API on 2026-08-27. Every rule carries its clause, the issue date of that text, and the regulation's own sentence; every conversion here was cross-checked against a millimetre figure printed in the regulation itself. This is NOT Indian law and NOT a certification — US federal accessibility requirements, offered for comparison and for projects to which they apply. Applicability is not modelled: a finding means 'if this rule applies, the geometry does not meet it'.

rules.note: ADA §404.2.3 governs CLEAR width — door open 90°, between the door face and the opposite stop — which is SMALLER than the structural opening a reconstruction measures, commonly by 50–75 mm. Structural width bounds clear width from above, so a shortfall here is certain and silence is NOT a pass. Treat a door near the figure as unresolved.

source.quote: Door openings shall provide a clear width of 32 inches (815 mm) minimum.

rules.note: Same clause and the same one-sided reading as the exit-door rule: the measured opening is structural, the regulated quantity is clear width, and only a shortfall is provable.

source.quote: Door openings shall provide a clear width of 32 inches (815 mm) minimum.

rules.note: A 1525 mm turning circle. The engine's room-width metric measures the widest usable circle, which is exactly this quantity. APPLICABILITY IS NOT MODELLED: §304.3.1 applies where a wheelchair must turn, and we cannot tell which rooms those are — the appliesTo list here is a guess at plausible rooms, not a legal determination. A cupboard failing this is not a violation.

source.quote: The turning space shall be a space of 60 inches (1525 mm) diameter minimum.

rules.note: Clear width of an accessible route. 36 CFR 1191 permits 815 mm at a short segment; this applies the 915 mm general figure everywhere, which over-asks at pinch points — the reviewer decides, not this check.

source.quote: Except as provided in 403.5.2 and 403.5.3, the clear width of walking surfaces shall be 36 inches (915 mm) minimum.
